title: Ben Zakkai
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in [Mishnah Sanhedrin 5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishnah_Sanhedrin.5.2): “An incident — Ben Zakkai examined the stems of figs.” In [the Gemara there (41a)](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.41a.24-28), the Gemara first supposes that this is not Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, and in the end concludes that Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai was then a student sitting before his teacher, and they called him Ben Zakkai; afterward, when he taught, they called him Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.[^1]

There is also a Ben Zakkai who was an Amora, as in [Chullin 52a (Hyman cites 53a)](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.52a.7): “Ulla reported in the name of Ben Zakkai … Rabbi Yochanan said”; but Hyman reports [Tosafot’s reading](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Chullin.52a.21.1) there as “Ulla ben Zakkai.” In [Semachot, chapter 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Tractate_Semachot.8.4): an incident with Yehudah and Hillel, the sons of Rabban Gamliel (son of Rabbi), who went in to Ben Zakkai in Babylonia; Hyman calls this a scribal error and proposes “to Rabbi Zakkai in Kabul.”[^2]

notes.text: The [continuation at Sanhedrin 41b](https://www.sefaria.org/Sanhedrin.41b.1) explains why the Mishnah calls the student Ben Zakkai. [Heilprin’s Mishnah entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1136&lang=en) refers the reader to Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

In the linked Chullin, Ulla transmits Ben Zakkai’s statement and Rabbi Yochanan gives a separate opinion. Tosafot writes “Ulla son of Rabbi Zakkai.” [Heilprin’s Chullin entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1137&lang=en) distinguishes the transmitter from the sage he quotes. The linked Semachot has Babylonia in Hebrew and Kabul in English. Hyman proposes reading Rabbi Zakkai in Kabul.
